result:
Done. I wrote a self-contained `CSVFormatAgentTest` (package `org.apache.commons.csv`) at `tests/org/apache/commons/csv/CSVFormatAgentTest.java`, covering:

- All 12 predefined formats' documented settings (`DEFAULT`, `EXCEL`, `RFC4180`, `TDF`, `MYSQL`, `ORACLE`, `POSTGRESQL_CSV/TEXT`, `INFORMIX_UNLOAD(_CSV)`, `MONGODB_CSV/TSV`) and the `Predefined` enum mapping
- `valueOf(String)` happy path plus `IllegalArgumentException`/`NullPointerException` boundary cases
- `newFormat(char)` defaults and its line-break rejection
- `Builder.create()`, `create(CSVFormat)`, `builder()`, `get()`/deprecated `build()` equivalence, and builder/format immutability
- Header and header-comments defensive copying, enum-based header, null/empty header semantics
- Delimiter, comment marker, escape, quote, null-string, max-rows setters including line-break rejection errors
- `equals`/`hashCode` contract (reflexive, null, wrong type, equal/unequal instances) and `toString` determinism
- `format(Object...)` quoting/escaping/null-substitution behavior
- `print(Object, Appendable, boolean)`, `println`, `printRecord`, `print`/`printer` resource-returning overloads (Appendable/File/Path), and `parse(Reader)`
- Package-private helpers documented in the javadoc: `copy()`, `copy(CSVFormat)`, `clone(T...)`, `getDelimiterCharArray()`, `getEscapeChar()`, `useMaxRows()`

`./compile.sh` reports `compiled OK`. I also removed the scratch javadoc-text files and build artifacts I created during analysis, leaving only the test class as a deliverable.
